acceptance.status_reason: THIS CRITERION FAILED ON FIRST MEASUREMENT AT removed=6 dead=2, AND THE REASON IS THE PART WORTH READING. The dead= limb requires the LIVE-READ value to be a single alphabetic token ending the line. Only the two ResourceNotFoundException lines matched; the four S3 lines read 'LIVE-READ: (404) Not Found'. I did not reformat them to fit the regex. I asked what the token was supposed to be and found a real defect in my own read: the order's step-1 template asks for '<NoSuchBucket | ResourceNotFoundException | the exact error code>', and '(404) Not Found' is an HTTP status line, not an error code. THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL -- head-bucket is a HEAD request, so the response carries no body and S3 transmits no error code at all; the CLI prints the bare status because that is all it received. Writing NoSuchBucket on the strength of a 404 would have been an INFERENCE presented as a measurement, which is what the claim-carrying rule forbids. So each bucket was RE-MEASURED with get-bucket-location, which is a GET and does transmit the code: opal-data-smartx and opal-code-smartx both returned rc=254 NoSuchBucket, and the positive control, get-bucket-location --bucket opal-data-news-v2 run as its own separate invocation, returned rc=0 with a LocationConstraint. The token in those lines is now measured on a call that can express it, and the instrument correction is recorded in the survey rather than quietly absorbed. The two /* lines are key patterns on those same two absent buckets; that annotation used to sit on the lines themselves and was moved to prose, because a machine-read line should end in its value and a key pattern has no existence of its own -- its read is its bucket's, which is why no separate call is reported for it and why the count is four ARNs over two buckets. ON GRAIN, WHICH A GRADER SHOULD CHECK: `REMOVED:` here means 'removed by the cell's RULE', which is what PHASE A measures, and it is NOT a claim about what PHASE B applied. For target 4 the two differ -- A3-r7 HELD the DynamoDB ARN and sent it to the CTO, so the rule removes it and the act did not -- and conversely the act removed arn:aws:s3:::codebuild-semantic-clustering-artifacts/*, which this list does not carry, precisely because the rule could not reach it. I deliberately did NOT rewrite the list to the PHASE B outcome: doing so would have erased this survey's central finding, which is the finding that produced A3-r7. POST_APPLY_narrow.md is the authority on what moved in the world; this file is the authority on what the rule yields; neither was rewritten to look like the other, and the survey now states that in a blockquote above the evidence. Base reading recorded by the issuer: MISSING: the survey, exit=2, so the test -f limb is live and this is not a stuck PASS.
